comments.body: Can we have a minute to draw attention to a new breakout room call that will be starting on Tues Jan 20th at 2pm UTC (and run on an every-other week basis) that focuses on shipping Fast Confirmation Rule.  If either @saltiniroberto or @mkalinin could lead the update, that would be great.

## Fork focus

As part of headliner proposals, we should explicitly [define the focus](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/community-consensus-fork-headliners-acd-working-groups/24088#p-58740-defining-the-fork-focus-4) for Hegotá.

* Scale L1
* Scale L2
* UX
* DX
* Decentralization
* [Resilience](https://x.com/VitalikButerin/status/2008174642066845778)

Examples from: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/community-consensus-fork-headliners-acd-working-groups/24088#p-58740-defining-the-fork-focus-4

> Scalability & Lower Fees: Meaningfully increase throughput, lower transaction costs, and unlock new use cases.
>
> Developer & User Experience: Simplify protocol complexity, enhance smart contract security, and reduce development friction.
>
> Security & Resilience: Strengthen the network’s security posture, enhance attack resistance, and mitigate emerging threats without compromising decentralization or censorship resistance.

I'd like to take a few minutes to describe an engine API change that I would like to propose for Glamsterdam. On calls to `notify_NewPayload` the engine should return not only the usual information of `VALID/INVALID/etc` but also a boolean indicating if the payload was censoring according to their view. 

Vanilla CLs then could ban the builder of that payload from any request they make. This entails changes in the CL and the EL. 
- On the CL side nodes have to add configurations to deal with this boolean. They could for example temporarily ban said builder, could keep track on how many times the builder is censoring, how many not censoring, etc. This should all be operator configurable. 
- On the EL side this should add heuristics to when to determine that a block was a censoring block. Most ELs already have some form of implementation of FOCIL and could reuse part of this feature. For example if they see a paying transaction in the mempool that has been there for 2 blocks and could have been appended in the end of the builder's block, they could declare that block as censoring. This should also be node operator configurable.

Glamsterdam: 

For SSZ progressive shape, there is slight preference from some people to shape the tree to the right. Affects the library work in EIP-7688 (but is a small change). If there's no strong preference for left, would like to swap to right and then lock it in that way.

- https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/11032/files
- https://github.com/ethereum/remerkleable/pull/16/files
- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4813/files

![](https://ethereum-magicians.org/uploads/default/original/3X/a/4/a41f4d5bb0f67344ec8d78117e047f7122bc0360.jpeg)

Also, EIP-7688 updated for v1.7.0-a.0 and ready for merge as well.

- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4630

Once merged, will update light client specs as those are still missing for Gloas.
